request.spec:
A year entry and a button generate the four calendar quarters of that year as periods named
<yyyy>-Q1 to <yyyy>-Q4, each as the period form would add it (a quarter that exists or overlaps is
left out); show how many were made.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A year entry and a button generate the four calendar quarters of that year as periods named
<yyyy>-Q1 to <yyyy>-Q4, each as the period form would add it (a quarter that exists or overlaps is
left out); show how many were made.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The periods screen now has a year box and a "Generate quarters" button. It creates the periods `<yyyy>-Q1` to `<yyyy>-Q4` and shows how many it made. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

- **What it creates:** each quarter runs from the first day of its first month to the last day of its third month. A quarter is skipped if a period on the sheet already has its name (ignoring case) or its dates overlap one. These are the same rules the period form uses. Each quarter that is made is written to the audit file as `PERIOD_ADDED`, in the same form as a period added by hand.
- **When it refuses:** a year that isn't four digits shows `period-generate-error` and changes nothing. Archived sheets and viewers are refused, the same as the existing generate buttons.
- **The count:** the result appears in the existing `period-generated` element, which the monthly and fiscal-year generators also use. The test reads that same element, so the three generators share one count and one error message. Pressing the button again clears the old count until the new one arrives.

**Server** (built the same way as the fiscal-year generator, reusing its save, audit and respond steps):
- `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/generate-quarters.POST.yml` (new endpoint)
- `period/BuildQuarterPeriods.java` and `period/GenerateQuartersRequest.java` (new)

**Front end:** `src/main/frontend/features/periods/Periods.tsx` has a new form with `period-generate-quarters-year` and `period-generate-quarters`.

The stored data didn't need to change, because the quarters are saved as ordinary periods.
